builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Free to Look, Free to Reason: Simple LLM Harnesses Outdiagnose Hand-Crafted Root Cause Analysis Agents
summary: The approach replaces hand-crafted RCA agents with fixed standard operating procedures, staged pipelines, and role agents by simple harnesses that prescribe none of the model's calls: a single call over an evidence package, a SQL agent, or the Codex coding agent. Cost is low and within constrained infrastructure, since mid-tier models suffice and higher reasoning effort changes accuracy by only a few points while multiplying time by up to seven; a stronger model mainly improves reliability, and a multi-turn harness mainly improves aptitude. Failure modes include possible dataset or evaluation bias toward the RCAtlas benchmark, dependence on the quality of the evidence package and tool access, and the risk that unconstrained investigation misses decisive evidence on failure modes not represented in the 90 validated cases.
rationale: For a team with one GPU or API access, dropping bespoke multi-agent RCA orchestration in favor of a simple harness on a mid-tier model is directly deployable, cheaper, and empirically more accurate on every model where both families were compared.
technique: Simple LLM harnesses for root cause analysis

claims.statement: The approach replaces hand-crafted RCA agents with fixed standard operating procedures, staged pipelines, and role agents by simple harnesses that prescribe none of the model's calls: a single call over an evidence package, a SQL agent, or the Codex coding agent. Cost is low and within constrained infrastructure, since mid-tier models suffice and higher reasoning effort changes accuracy by only a few points while multiplying time by up to seven; a stronger model mainly improves reliability, and a multi-turn harness mainly improves aptitude. Failure modes include possible dataset or evaluation bias toward the RCAtlas benchmark, dependence on the quality of the evidence package and tool access, and the risk that unconstrained investigation misses decisive evidence on failure modes not represented in the 90 validated cases.

Simple harnesses achieve PR@1 65-77% on three mid-tier models versus 16-53% for published hand-crafted RCA agents and 6-39% for non-LLM methods; every Pareto-optimal run in cost or time among runs more accurate than the best non-LLM method uses a simple harness.
